source_prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building accessibility checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Write the date and time of the inspection.
3. Document the name of the building and its address.
4. Include the names and qualifications of the inspectors.
5. List the specific accessibility standards that apply, such as the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA) guidelines.
6. Identify and describe each area that failed the inspection, including elevators, ramps, doorways, restrooms, signage, and parking spaces.
7. Record which standards were not met in each area with detailed notes about deficiencies. Use precise measurements and locations when applicable.
8. Include photographs or sketches that clearly show the issues.
9. Note any potential hazards for individuals with disabilities resulting from failed checks.
10. Provide recommendations for correcting the accessibility issues, including any relevant codes or guidelines.
11. Indicate whether the failed checks are critical to safety and require immediate correction.
12. If known, document the timeline for when corrections can be expected.
13. Record any communication with building
